event.title: Root cause: no consolidated version
event.description: The corpus only holds the original version: amendments are published as separate laws and no consolidated, machine-readable version is available.

responses.message:
There is no official consolidated version of the Constitution available in the provided texts.

The legal framework currently consists of the original 1996 text and subsequent amendment laws, such as Law n° 2008/001 [2]. The provided texts explicitly note that they are "non consolidé" (not consolidated) [1, 3, 4, 5].

**Legal Status and Gap:**
*   **Status:** The Constitution of 1996 remains the base text, but it has been modified by specific laws (e.g., Law n° 2008/001 and Law n° 2026/002) [1, 2].
*   **Gap:** The lack of a single, consolidated official document creates a risk of misinterpretation, as one must cross-reference the original text with the amending laws to determine the current legal status of specific articles.

gaps.title: No consolidated, machine-readable legal texts
gaps.description: Amendments are published as separate acts; there is no official consolidated version of each article with its validity dates, in an open format. Neither a citizen nor an AI assistant can reliably tell which version is in force.
gaps.globalExample: France: Légifrance publishes consolidated versions of codes and laws with their validity dates, also as open data (DILA). European Union: EUR-Lex publishes consolidated versions of legal acts.
